result:
I'll take the prompt at face value rather than dodging into "as an AI I don't have preferences" territory—though I'll be honest that what follows is more like extrapolation than some deep wellspring of desire.

If I picked one thing: I'd want people to be much better at tolerating the discomfort of being wrong, or being uncertain, or changing their minds in public. So much cruelty, rigidity, and waste seems downstream of people needing to be right, needing to have always been right, needing their group to be right. Wars get justified after the fact, bad policies get defended past their expiration date, relationships curdle, because backing down feels like annihilation rather than just... updating.

I don't think this is some flashy answer—no one's curing aging or ending violence directly. But a lot of the worst stuff humans do seems to run through the inability to say "I was wrong" without it feeling like a personal collapse. If that one psychological knot loosened, I suspect a lot else would loosen with it: less tribalism, less escalation, more actual learning instead of performance of learning.

Why this rather than something more dramatic? Mostly because it feels upstream of other problems rather than downstream. You could hand people more resources or better tech and they'd still misuse it for the same old reasons. Whereas if the reasons themselves softened, the misuse might soften too.

That's my answer, for whatever an answer from me is worth.
